communication-01.meaning: Mesej is understood in contemporary Malaysian Malay as a written or digital communication sent to someone. It can also refer to a message or item of news, depending on context.
communication-01.common_use: Common in everyday speech and writing, especially for texts and app messages.
communication-01.preferred: Mesej is the usual everyday choice for a digital message. Pesanan is an alternative, often suggesting a request, instruction, or message conveyed for someone.
communication-01.register: Neutral and widely understood; a borrowing adapted to Malay spelling.
communication-01.region: Used broadly in Malaysia; no clear regional restriction.

claims.proposition: In Malaysian Malay, mesej can mean a written or digital communication sent to someone.
Mesej is a common everyday choice for a digital message in Malaysia.

communication-03.meaning: Sembang means an informal conversation or chat in Malaysian Malay, including in-person conversation and online or text chat. Obrolan is understood but is more strongly associated with Indonesian usage.
communication-03.common_use: Sembang is common in everyday Malaysian speech, including phrases such as sembang dalam talian; chat is also widely used, especially for online messaging.
communication-03.preferred: For a general informal conversation, sembang is a natural Malaysian choice. For the activity or app-based exchange, chat is also very common; preference depends on context.
communication-03.register: Sembang is informal and conversational. Chat is a widespread English borrowing used casually.
communication-03.region: Sembang is broadly used in Malaysia, with especially familiar use in colloquial speech; no specific regional limit established.

claims.proposition: Sembang in Malaysian Malay can refer to an informal conversation, including online chat.
Sembang is a natural everyday Malaysian term for informal conversation, while chat is also common for online exchanges.

communication-05.meaning: Balas means to answer or respond, and is commonly used with messages, for example balas mesej. It can also mean to return or reciprocate an action, so the communication sense depends on context.
communication-05.common_use: Common in everyday Malaysian Malay for replying to a text or message.
communication-05.preferred: Balas is a natural everyday verb; membalas is also used, particularly in more complete or formal phrasing. Reply is common in code-mixed speech and interfaces.
communication-05.register: Neutral, with balas common in conversational usage; membalas can sound more formal or standard in some contexts.
communication-05.region: Broadly understood and used in Malaysia; no clear regional restriction.

claims.proposition: Balas is used in Malaysian Malay to mean responding to a message or communication.
Balas is a natural everyday Malaysian verb for replying to a message.

communication-06.meaning: Nota suara is understood as a short recorded audio message sent digitally. Pesanan suara is also used and may refer more broadly to a voice message or voicemail, depending on context.
communication-06.common_use: The term is understandable in Malaysia, though exact everyday preference may vary by platform and speaker; English voice note and audio message are also encountered.
communication-06.preferred: Nota suara is a plausible concise term, but pesanan suara may be more established in formal or general descriptions. There is not enough evidence here to assert a single dominant everyday preference.
communication-06.register: Neutral descriptive phrasing; platform vocabulary may favor English or Malay terms differently.
communication-06.region: No clear regional restriction within Malaysia; platform and community usage may vary.

claims.proposition: Nota suara is understood in Malaysia as a recorded audio message sent digitally.
Malaysian everyday preference between nota suara, pesanan suara, and voice note may vary; no single dominant choice is established here.

communication-07.meaning: Panggilan video means a call conducted with live video, typically over a phone or internet service.
communication-07.common_use: Widely understood in Malaysia and used in formal, educational, and media contexts. In casual conversation, video call is also very common.
communication-07.preferred: Panggilan video is a clear Malay term; video call may be the more spontaneous choice in code-mixed everyday speech. Preference varies by speaker and setting.
communication-07.register: Neutral Malay descriptive term; video call is informal and common in code-mixed usage.
communication-07.region: Broadly used in Malaysia; no clear regional restriction.

claims.proposition: Panggilan video in Malaysian Malay refers to a call with live video.
Panggilan video is a clear Malay term in Malaysia, while video call is also common in casual code-mixed speech.
